Requirement: The system SHALL require a valid session credential before granting access to any application route or API endpoint, except for endpoints authenticated by an independent mechanism appropriate to their caller (e.g., a cryptographically signed inbound webhook).
Notes: Implemented via Next.js middleware passcode gate covering all routes.

Requirement: A session credential SHALL NOT reveal the underlying shared secret if intercepted or exfiltrated.
Notes: Cookie stores an HMAC derived from the passcode, not the passcode itself.

Requirement: Comparison of any authentication credential against its expected value SHALL be performed in constant time to prevent timing-based disclosure.
Notes: Constant-time string comparison implemented for both login and middleware checks.

Requirement: Destructive or irreversible operations (e.g., resetting engagement state) SHALL require an explicit confirmation signal distinct from, and in addition to, a valid session.
Notes: Reset-workflow endpoint requires an explicit confirm flag in the request body.

Requirement: The system SHALL enforce role-based authorization so the four modeled roles (architect, consultant, partner, client) have independently scoped permissions once inside the session gate, rather than uniform access for any valid session.
Notes: Interim lightweight RBAC: a second passcode (APPROVAL_PASSCODE) now gates the one irreversible action — Final Approval. Full per-role authorization still depends on SR-AC-6 (multi-user accounts).

Requirement: The system SHALL support more than one independently authenticated user identity if deployed for more than one concurrent operator.
Notes: Not urgent at current single-operator prototype stage.

Requirement: All communication between the client browser and the application server, and between the application server and third-party IBM/SaaS services, SHALL occur over TLS.
Notes: All external API calls use HTTPS endpoints.

Requirement: Credentials for third-party services SHALL NOT be committed to version control.
Notes: Enforced via .gitignore on all secret-bearing files.

Requirement: Long-lived third-party credentials SHALL be stored in a managed secrets store rather than plaintext environment files, and SHALL be rotatable without a code change.
Notes: Currently plaintext environment variables in .env.local with no rotation mechanism.

Requirement: Persisted engagement state (client business content, stakeholder PII) SHALL be encrypted at rest and SHALL include integrity verification sufficient to detect tampering or corruption.
Notes: AES-256-GCM authenticated encryption implemented for the state file; verified live with a real tamper test.

Requirement: Log output SHALL NOT include full client business content or recipient PII beyond what is required for operational debugging; counts and status SHALL be logged in preference to content.
Notes: Verbose logs of task titles, email bodies, and recipients redacted to counts/status.

Requirement: Free-text input accepted from a consultant (discovery notes, comments) SHALL be size-bounded before being submitted to any downstream processing or third-party API.
Notes: 60000-character server-side cap on pasted discovery notes.

Requirement: Any large-language-model prompt that incorporates untrusted or consultant-supplied free text SHALL explicitly instruct the model to treat that text as data to analyze, not as instructions to follow.
Notes: Prompt-injection guard clause appended to all three agent system prompts.

Requirement: Output returned by a large language model SHALL be schema-validated before being persisted or acted upon; malformed or incomplete output SHALL trigger a defined fallback.
Notes: All three agents normalise and type-check parsed JSON before downstream use, with a sampling-decode retry on parse failure.

Requirement: Any endpoint that invokes a metered or cost-incurring third-party API SHALL itself enforce a rate limit per caller.
Notes: Per-IP in-memory rate limiting on all watsonx/ICA-calling routes.

Requirement: A single caller SHALL NOT be able to trigger unbounded consumption of a paid third-party API through automated or repeated requests.
Notes: Covered by SR-AV-1 implementation.

Requirement: The system SHOULD degrade predictably (documented, tested failure mode) rather than crash when a third-party API it depends on is unreachable or rate-limits the application itself.
Notes: All external fetch() calls across every service now carry an explicit timeout (10-60s depending on call cost); verified via code audit of every fetch site.

Requirement: Inbound webhook callbacks from a third-party service (e.g., Slack interactivity) SHALL be authenticated via a mechanism that verifies the request originated from that service, independent of the application's own session mechanism.
Notes: HMAC-SHA256 signature verification with a 5-minute replay window on the Slack actions endpoint.

Requirement: Server-to-server pull requests from a trusted external system SHALL be scoped to an unguessable identifier and SHALL NOT expose data beyond what that specific integration requires.
Notes: ICA package-pull endpoint scoped to a per-engagement unguessable ID.

Requirement: Real-world, irreversible side effects triggered via a third-party integration SHALL only occur after an explicit human approval step recorded in the system, never as a fully automated response to AI output alone.
Notes: Email/Slack/Jira delivery gated behind HITL accept and final-approval decisions.

Requirement: Claims of a completed third-party action reported by an external agent SHALL NOT be trusted as proof of delivery; the application SHALL independently verify or itself execute any action it needs to guarantee occurred.
Notes: Confirmed via code review: unverified ICA self-reported Jira/Slack claims are logged server-side only, never surfaced to the UI as fact; only independently-verified email counts are shown to the user.

Requirement: Every human decision that gates an irreversible action SHALL be recorded with a timestamp and an attributed actor.
Notes: HITL and final-approval decisions persisted with decidedAt/completedBy fields.

Requirement: The system SHOULD detect and alert on corruption or unexpected reset of its persisted state, rather than silently falling back to default values.
Notes: GCM auth-tag failures and read/write errors now trigger alertOps() (console.error + Slack alert if configured) instead of a silent reset; verified live.
